A1.justification: Both PDFs contain 37 pages of the same Unified Preference Optimization work, including matching figures, tables, equations and Appendix A. A localized layout overlap in v4 does not prevent recovering and comparing the underlying text.

before.justification: v3 reports original UPO experiments on LLaMA and Pythia models, including alignment scores, safety/readability evaluations, ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains the original UPO experiments and their reported outcomes in the main text and Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: The UPO objective, advantage-weighted likelihood update, expectile value regression and Algorithm 1 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both retain the Anthropic HH, OpenAssistant and SHP dialogue data, with the same safety, readability and supplementary verbosity evaluations. No dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and supplementary experiments, including MODPO, A-LOL, aoPPO and DRO-V in Tables 2–3 and ConDPO in Table 15.

E3.justification: The reported model configurations, training settings, 512-prompt evaluation, toxicity thresholds and testing procedures remain unchanged, including Appendix A.3.

E4.justification: The hyperparameter, instability, readability, objective-tradeoff, random-reward and qualitative case analyses in Sections 5.3–5.4 and Appendix A.4 are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: The same uncertainty values and reporting practices, significance claims and statistical information are retained. No run-count, seed or uncertainty-estimation information is added or removed.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends and displayed responses are unchanged. However, Section 5.2 drops the explicit qualitative finding that UPO equals or surpasses the chosen response's quality, replacing the closing comparative summary with an incomplete sentence.

T1.justification: Definition 1, the UPO derivations, Theorems A.1–A.3 and the supplementary mathematical analyses are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and Section 6 retain the same claims about combining preference and auxiliary objectives, training stability, efficiency and alignment performance.

C2.justification: Explanations concerning sparse rewards, conflicting preferences, gradient instability and evaluation bias are retained, as are the stated limitations. Section 5.3's wording edits preserve its Pareto-front interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 retains the same implementation code, value-head architecture, hyperparameters, hardware, runtimes and GPT-4 evaluation prompt. The new review link does not change code or data access.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The publication notice and OpenReview link add publication metadata rather than related research.

P1.justification: v4 adds publication/review notices and makes small wording edits in Section 5.3. Section 5.2's closing sentence becomes grammatically incomplete: 'our technique qualitatively past approaches.' The section structure is retained.

P2.justification: Publication headers and front matter cause early-page text reflow. Figures and tables are retained, but Figure 4's placement in v4 obscures the end of the sentence specifying that readability is evaluated on the entire evaluation set.

improvement.justification: The publication/review metadata adds provenance, while the method, theory, numerical evidence and appendices remain unchanged. The incomplete sentence in Section 5.2 and Figure 4's overlap with evaluation-scope text introduce limited but clear losses in readability and precision.
